basis: Malignancy arising in the supraglottic larynx, part of the respiratory airway.
ETFDH-related metabolic disease; lipid-storage myopathy predominates (>50%). Severe neonatal cardiac and hepatic involvement is less typical.
Developmental delay, skeletal anomalies and congenital heart defects define syndrome; renal dysplasia/obstruction 30-79%; frequent ptosis omitted because of cap.
Clonal myeloid malignancy occupying marrow and blood; extramedullary organ involvement is not established as common.
Predominantly pure cerebellar neurodegeneration; additional manifestations remain within the neurologic axis.
Mast-cell-mediated inflammatory wheals of skin; local vascular permeability does not establish cardiovascular disease.
Inherited arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Definition specifies isolated disease; keratoderma and woolly hair lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
Hereditary abnormal tooth morphology; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Retinal degeneration characterizes both listed subtypes; systemic Bardet-Biedl manifestations are not established as common across this umbrella.
Inherited retinal cone dysfunction with impaired visual acuity, color vision and characteristic electroretinographic abnormalities.
Primary congenital microcephaly with neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures; short stature alone does not establish another damaged organ.
Syndromic intellectual disability; short stature, facial dysmorphism and clinodactyly do not establish additional functional organ damage.
Poststreptococcal immune disease defined by carditis and arthritis; immune-mediated chorea is a major Jones criterion. Transient rash/nodules excluded.
Childhood steroid-sensitive glomerular disease, usually immune-mediated minimal-change podocytopathy; proteinuria defines renal dysfunction.
Isolated inherited sensorineural hearing loss, documented in 11/11 patients.
Structural separation of the vitreous from the retina; both structures belong to the ocular axis.
Congenital humoral immunodeficiency involving B-cell development or function; subsequent infections are separate diseases.
Congenital inward eyelid malposition, potentially damaging the cornea; eyelids and cornea share the ocular axis.
Gallstones within the common bile duct; extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Subcutaneous fat loss with insulin resistance and dyslipidemia. Hypertension is separately coded; raised CK and hepatomegaly alone do not establish organ damage.
Cavernous vascular malformations located in the brain; intracranial hemorrhage occurs in 11/43 (~26%) and adds no further axis.
Melanoma originating in the ocular ciliary body; metastatic organ involvement is not intrinsic to this concept.
Myelin-defect neuropathy with congenital contractures; pulmonary hypoplasia 3/9 (33%); ptosis/strabismus 1/1 assessed, with limited frequency evidence.
EBV-associated epithelial infection and hyperplasia of oral mucosa; associated HIV infection is a separate disease.
Ptosis, neurodevelopmental delay and metopic/craniosynostosis abnormalities define syndrome; hearing and cardiac abnormalities are each under 30%.
